---
title: "Quickstart: first generation on a Tesla T4"
description: "Run your first Stokastisk inference on Kaggle: load Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct with the Triton attention backend, generate text, chat, and release both GPUs."
guide-section: "Get started"
---

After [installing](installation.qmd), run engine code in an ordinary notebook cell. The model downloads from Hugging Face on first use.

```python
from stokastisk import LLM, StokastiskConfig

config = StokastiskConfig(max_model_len=2048)             # one T4, FP16, TRITON_ATTN

with LLM("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", config=config) as llm:
    print(llm.verify_attention_backend())                 # TRITON_ATTN
    print(llm.complete("The capital of France is", max_tokens=16))
    reply = llm.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words."}])
    print(reply[0].outputs[0].text)
```

`with` releases the GPUs on exit. Without it, call `llm.close()`.

::: {.callout-note}
## Evidence
This pattern ran on Kaggle in notebook 18 (plain cells) and notebook 16 (script form) on build 3. See [Kaggle notebooks and evidence](kaggle-examples.qmd).
:::

## Running as a script

vLLM starts its engine in a spawned process, so in a **script** keep engine code under a main guard:

```python
%%writefile main.py
import stokastisk


def main():
    config = stokastisk.StokastiskConfig(max_model_len=2048)
    with stokastisk.LLM("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", config=config) as llm:
        print(llm.verify_attention_backend())
        print(llm.complete("The capital of France is", max_tokens=16))


if __name__ == "__main__":      # required: vLLM spawns processes that re-import the script
    main()
```

```bash
!python main.py
```

## Which model fits?

Each T4 has about 15 GiB. FP16 weights take about 2 bytes per parameter, plus KV cache.

| Model size | Use |
|---|---|
| up to about 3B | one GPU, `tensor_parallel_size=1` (fastest) |
| about 7B (14 GiB of weights) | both GPUs, `tensor_parallel_size=2` |

Ask the SDK instead of guessing: `stokastisk.recommend_parallelism(...)` ([Parallelism](parallelism.qmd)) and `stokastisk.check_model(...)` ([Diagnostics](diagnostics-compatibility.qmd)), which reports whether that exact checkpoint was ever run on Kaggle.

## What you will see

`Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference` warnings on the first request are informational (a one-time latency spike). The first engine start downloads the model weights from Hugging Face.
